title: Sunny Deol Stays Fit at 68 With Samosas, Desi Ghee, and Two Hours of Daily Exercise
excerpt: The Border 2 star follows no diet plan — just old-school Punjabi food, daily swimming, weight training, and a 5:30 AM wake-up call that hasn't changed in decades.
body:
• Bollywood veteran Sunny Deol, 68, credits one to two hours of daily exercise — including weight training, swimming, squash, and pranayama — for maintaining his action-hero physique.
  • The actor follows no strict diet plan, instead eating simple home-cooked Punjabi meals including desi ghee parathas, samosas, and roti with homemade butter.
  • Deol wakes before sunrise daily, emphasizing that early rising and consistent physical activity foster positive thinking and sustained energy.
  • Currently riding high on the success of Border 2, the Gadar star says he still "feels like a young hero" and has no plans to slow down.

Sunny Deol has never needed a nutritionist's spreadsheet or a biohacker's supplement stack. At 68, the man who made "dhai kilo ka haath" a national catchphrase still looks like he could rip out a handpump — and his secret is disarmingly old-school: move your body every single day, eat what your mother cooked, and get up before the sun does.

In a recent interview, the Border 2 star laid out his approach to fitness with characteristic bluntness. "I don't follow any strict diet. I stick to simple, home-cooked meals," Deol said. "I don't really think much about food."

The Workout: No Shortcuts, No Excuses

Deol's daily routine begins at 5:30 AM with swimming, followed by a weight training session that typically runs one to two hours. He supplements the gym work with sports — squash, table tennis, and weekend hikes — and devotes a full hour to pranayama breathing exercises each day. "Fitness is an addiction for me," Deol has said in past interviews. "If I don't work out, I don't feel energetic through the day."

The actor recently shared photos from a workout session on Instagram showing him grinding through barbell shoulder presses and biceps curls. His caption was characteristically direct: "No excuses! Stay Fit, Stay Happy."

The Diet: Desi Ghee, Samosas, and Zero Guilt

While the fitness industry pushes restrictive meal plans and protein-powder regimens, Deol's diet reads like a Punjabi household menu. Breakfast is scrambled eggs and fruit, often blended into a homemade apple-yogurt shake. Lunch leans toward grilled chicken with spinach, broccoli, and carrots — occasionally swapped for pasta with chicken.

Dinner is where his Punjabi roots take over: desi roti slathered with homemade butter and washed down with lassi. On shoot days, he treats himself to samosas and paneer pakoras with green chutney. "I ended up eating samosas, desi ghee parathas," Deol said with a laugh. "I don't aim for a bulky body."

"Fitness keeps you healthy and fosters positive thinking. Those who wake up early and go to bed early see the world differently."

— Sunny Deol

The Philosophy: Activity Over Aesthetics

Deol's fitness philosophy is rooted in his childhood — he was a school and college athlete across football, badminton, tennis, cricket, and athletics before Bollywood came calling. He credits his father Dharmendra, himself a fitness icon well into his eighties, as a primary influence. "Even after eating more, I never gained weight because I was always so active with sports," Deol explained.

It's an approach that stands in stark contrast to the current Bollywood obsession with six-pack transformations and dramatic physical overhauls. Deol's consistency — decades of daily workouts rather than months of crash training for a role — offers a different model entirely.

What's Next

Deol is currently riding the success of Border 2, the sequel to the 1997 war drama that cemented his place as Bollywood's quintessential action hero. He also has the period drama Lahore 1947, directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and produced by Aamir Khan, in the pipeline. At 68, he shows no signs of stepping back from physically demanding roles — or from his morning samosa-and-chai ritual.
nri_angle: Deol's approach to fitness — rooted in traditional Punjabi food culture and daily discipline rather than Western diet trends — resonates with diaspora audiences navigating health advice across cultures.
